chunks: And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What is the least distance at which the traveler shortens (his prayer)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'A Bareyd.'

key_terms.بَرِيدٌ: A unit of distance (approx. 12 miles/4 farsakhs)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum distance a Muslim must travel to qualify for shortening prayers?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from al-Kafi defines the threshold for the legal status of a traveler (musafir) by specifying 'Bareyd' as the minimum distance for shortening prayers. Historically, this establishes the baseline for the fiqh of qasr, distinguishing it from the distance required for full shortening (typically 8 farsakhs), thereby anchoring the practical application of ritual flexibility in early Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘The least of what the traveler would be shortening (his Salāt) in?’ So heasws said: ‘A Bareyd (12 miles approx.)’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is a narration from him (narrator of previous Hadith) by his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Ayyub who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the minimum distance after the traveling of which a traveler reduces his Salah (prayer). He (the Imam) said, ‘It is one barid.’”
